title: Volume 1 Chapter 2: Nail Machine 2
content: The next day.
I regretted my own words of “bring whatever you want” almost immediately.
“I couldn’t choose, so I brought them all☆ Ehehe☆”
It wasn’t a simple “ehehe.”
Inside the cosmetic pouch Sayori brought were rows of small bottles of nail polish.
It had seemed like a lot of work when she brought the magazine, but this was quite heavy too.
“Hey, how many of these are there?”
“Um, probably around fifty?”
That’s way too many.
“When I look at cosmetics, there are so many cute polishes in the nail section that I can’t help but buy them! I thought, if I try painting, it might just work out! Hehe☆”
It wasn’t just “hehe.”
The polishes were all unused and new—but not entirely. Some had a little paint missing. They were probably evidence of Sayori’s past trial and error.
On the other hand, there were many unopened ones. Did she buy them on impulse, driven by the principle of cuteness?

—Well, even modelers sometimes get asked by people unrelated to the hobby, “What do you use models for? Just to display them on a shelf?” Especially since I’m the type of modeler who is satisfied just displaying them once I’ve made them, that’s pretty accurate.
For Sayori, keeping those colorful bottles might feel like gazing at completed models.
That said, today would be the end of just collecting and admiring them.
“So, which one should we paint!?”
With a cheerful expression, Sayori began to line up the bottles on the desk.

Even though they’re all called nail polish, the colors and textures vary greatly. There are soft pastel colors, foundation colors that match skin tones, elegant pearl colors with a refined shine, and glittery ones. There are just too many options.
“I’ll paint whatever you want. Today is just about painting.”
Compared to grinding nails, the process is quick.
“Ehh~? No way~! I can’t choose~!”
Grinning, Sayori picked up the bottles and compared them.
She seemed to be having fun just choosing. I understood her feelings well since I always struggle in front of many colors when selecting paint for models.
“Hey, Azuma-kun, you choose!”
“Huh!? Me!?”
“Yeah, yeah! What color do you like? If it’s not here, I can find it, so pick a color you want to paint!”
Sayori even brought the fashion magazine I had left in the garage.
She showed me the nail polish catalog.
“Come on, come on, just say your favorite color!”
This girl really seems to be having fun.
“Well, even if you say that... I can’t really tell the differences...”
“Oh, they say guys can recognize fewer colors than girls...”
It’s true that they say men can recognize fewer colors.
“Not really? I can recognize them just fine. I have lots of paint for models. There are various shades of white, and I mix colors too.”
“Oh! So you do have a preference for colors!”
“Models and fashion are different...”
Besides, it’s not for my own fashion. It’s for Sayori.
“I have no idea what colors would suit you, Sayori.”
“...Are you trying to pick a color that suits me, Azuma-kun?”
“Well, of course. It’s your nails, Sayori.”
I looked at the bottles and pondered what to do.
Maybe something flashy with glitter would be better—but Sayori usually wears flashy clothes and accessories, so maybe a more subdued color that wouldn’t clash would be better?
I had no idea!
“Hehe♪”
Sayori seemed to find it amusing that I was struggling to decide, covering her mouth as she laughed.
“...What’s so funny?”
“Nothing, nothing! Just take your time choosing! A color that suits me!”
“Yeah, yeah... it would be easier if this were model paint.”
I unintentionally voiced my true feelings, and Sayori’s previously cheerful demeanor shifted to a glare.
“I’m not a model, you know!”
“I know that.”
“Azuma-kun, you can’t say things like that to other girls, even if you think it!”
“? What are you talking about?”
“Nothing at all! Hurry up and choose!”
It seems a gal’s mood can change in an instant.
(You say to take your time, then hurry up and choose...)
I’m used to handling models, and I thought I had a good grasp on nails by now.
But when it comes to dealing with girls, I still have no idea.
I’m left anxious, wondering why her mood changed.
As I looked at the bottles of polish, I found one with a rare color.
“This is a holographic color, isn’t it?”
“Oh, wow, you know about it!”
I picked up a deep purple holographic nail polish without thinking.
“This is amazing! I found it on SNS, and I was so surprised! It changes color depending on how the light hits it! Isn’t that just crazy!?”
“Yeah, I guess so.”

Holographic colors are strange paints that change hue depending on the angle and the way light hits them. For example, this polish is purple, but at different angles, it can appear pink, red, or bluish.
When it comes to high-end paints used for cars, the way they shine can change dramatically, radiating a rainbow-like glow.
“I made a model with a holographic color too.”
“Really? No way! I want to see!”
“Second shelf from the bottom in that showcase.”
Sayori immediately stood up and peeked at my model display shelf.
I had felt that the holographic color of the car my father showed me was cool, so I painted a model with the same color scheme.
“Wow~! It really shines... so stylish! You made all of these, right, Azuma-kun?”
“Of course.”
“Wow, your dexterity is insane... I don’t really get it, but it’s amazing! It’s incredible!”
Her tail wagged back and forth.
Sayori often uses words like “amazing,” “incredible,” and “cool,” but it’s convenient to see how much she thinks it’s amazing by the movement of her tail.
“...Do you know the anime that features that machine?”
“I have no idea! But I know you’re amazing!”
“Is that so?”

Oh no. That machine is one that the protagonist only piloted once in the series, equipped with special beam-reflecting armor, and I recreated it in holographic color. In the anime, it didn’t get much action, but in the movie, it made a big comeback— I felt the urge to explain everything.
It’s a bad habit of an otaku.
“Hmm, oh, wow.”
Sayori started doing a strange dance in front of the showcase.
No, she wasn’t dancing; I could tell she was checking the model’s holographic color from various angles, but to an outsider, it looked like a peculiar dance.
Since holographic colors change depending on how light hits them, they can be maximized in complex designs with many curves—like cars or robot models.
“If you like this color, should we go with this one♪”
Eventually, Sayori began to say that.
“...Is it really okay to choose so easily?”
“Because it’s your favorite color, right? So let’s just try painting it!”
Sayori was grinning.
Honestly, I had been wanting to paint with a holographic color too. It felt a bit embarrassing, as if she could see through my inner thoughts.
It’s true.
Nails painted with holographic colors will change their hues depending on the angle, lighting, or sunlight.
“I’ll be so happy every time I see my nails painted this color! So—yeah, this color is good!”
If she’s saying that much...
“Alright, let’s go with this.”
“Yay! Azuma-kun, you’re finally going to paint for me!”
“Yeah. It’s been a long time coming.”
Just applying paint to her nails—that simple act had been something Sayori couldn’t do until now.
I could only imagine how happy she must be.
“—I’ll make sure to do it right.”
“Okay♪ I’m counting on you♪”
Sayori sat across from me.
She looked relaxed and seemed to have nothing on her mind, just like usual. Well, that’s fine for Sayori.
On the other hand, I took a deep breath and exhaled.
(...Please don’t let me fail.)
I believed that painting models was a one-shot deal.
While some corrections are possible, and I know how to do them, I’d prefer to paint cleanly and evenly with as few steps as possible.
From what I’ve researched, nail polish is similar. It’s not just about painting with a brush.
“Alright, let’s do this.”
Sayori extended her right hand.
I took her hand and adjusted the position of her fingers to support her hand for easier painting.
I swallowed hard.
“Ah, Azuma-kun, you’re nervous, aren’t you?”
“Shut up.”
I already knew that without being told.
I opened the cap of the polish. The brush on the underside was loaded with paint.
There was too much paint, so I hooked the brush on the bottle’s opening to adjust the amount.
Then, I placed the brush on Sayori’s nail at a forty-five-degree angle.
I created a tiny gap between the nail and the brush, consciously letting the paint flow into that space.
I painted the center once, then once on each side, right and left.
Finally, I added the leftover paint to the tip of her nail—and...
Just painting one nail made me let out a huge sigh.
“Wow, Azuma-kun, it’s amazing for your first time!”
Sayori’s thumb nail was painted with a dazzling purple holographic color. It seemed the paint contained glitter, enhancing the holographic effect.
For a first attempt, I thought it was pretty good.
(But still, this nail polish brush is hard to use...)
Since the handle is integrated with the cap, I couldn’t maneuver it as I wanted.
I usually use a fine brush for painting models. I only use it for small details like robot twin eyes or armor details.
If I’m painting a larger area like nails, I’d use an airbrush.
(Should I use a fine brush...?)
There’s no necessity to use the brush that comes with the bottle, so I should consider that for the future.
For now, I decided to use the nail polish brush. I painted her thumb, then her index, middle, and ring fingers in order.
After doing it a few times, I felt like I was starting to get the hang of it.
And so, I applied paint to all of Sayori’s fingers—
“Done~!”
Sayori spread her five fingers and gazed at them.
The holographic polish was applied to all of Sayori’s nails.
“It looks amazing! As expected of Azuma-kun... but why do you look so down!?”
Meanwhile, I was holding my face in despair.
“No... I messed up a bit on the left middle finger... and I’m worried about the unevenness on the right pinky.”
“You can’t even tell! It looks great!”
“Really...?”
I felt more strongly that I could have done better.
I should definitely use a fine brush next time.
But the nail polish dries quickly. If I take it out of the bottle and paint carefully, the paint might dry halfway through.
It might be faster to get used to the brush that comes with the bottle.
“F-fufu...”
As I held my head in my hands, thinking about this and that,
For some reason, Sayori started laughing.
“Hey, don’t laugh in front of someone who’s feeling down.”
I joked as I said that.
“Oh, no, no! It’s not that I’m laughing at your mistakes. I was just a bit surprised, or rather, I had a realization?”
“A realization?”
“That Azuma-kun can make mistakes too.”
“Of course I can...”
What is she talking about?
Is there anyone who doesn’t make mistakes?
“There are plenty of failed models and junk parts lying around in the back warehouse. Also, the ones I don’t want to display outside.”
“Really!? I want to see!”
“I’m not showing you! They’re failures!”
“Ehh!”
Sayori pouted in dissatisfaction.
Does she really want to see my failed models? Is she secretly a bit mean?
“Isn’t it proof of all the hard work you’ve put in, Azuma-kun!? Show me!”
“No.”
Sayori looked disappointed for a moment, but then her face brightened.
“Hmm... well, whatever! For now, let’s celebrate your first nail! Can I take a picture and show it to my friends?”
“That’s fine, I guess.”
Sayori took out her smartphone and started taking pictures of her nails.
Click, click, click, click, click—the shutter sound kept going. How many is she planning to take?
“Ehehe...”
Comparing the photos with her own hands, Sayori was grinning.
“Ah—no! I can’t stop grinning! I’m too happy~!”
“Is it really that much?”
“Of course! And also—”
Sayori spread her five fingers, turning her palm toward me.
“The fact that you’re feeling down about making mistakes means... you still want to get better, right? Just thinking about how your nails will look next time makes me so excited!”
“Seriously, you...”
It’s so typical of Sayori to take everything positively.
But I couldn’t deny it either. I didn’t want to remain clumsy.
I wanted to get better at painting.
“...Well, I’ll leave it at that.”
“You’re not being honest♪ But I’m looking forward to the nails you’ll do for me!”
“If you have a nail design in mind for next time, let me know. I’ll study it.”
“Okay♪ I’ll think about it♪”
This first nail session was probably coming to a close.
I didn’t know when the next time would be, but it should last for about two weeks, and during that time, I could focus on making models.
I wondered if the knowledge I gained from nails could be applied to models.
I didn’t have any ideas yet, but thinking about it must mean that the nail work had stimulated me in some way.
“Thanks again, my nail artist!”
“Yeah, yeah. I look forward to your next visit.”
I joked as I said that.
Sayori waved her freshly painted hand cheerfully as she left the garage.
Sayori would come again, but that would be a while from now.
The garage felt quiet without Sayori, a bit lonely, but—
For model work, that was the most convenient situation.
(For an introvert, this is much more calming.)
I told myself that as I tidied up my desk.
I wondered when Sayori would come again—thinking about such things.
“Sorry~! Azuma-kun! Help me!”
As it turned out, the next time Sayori came to the garage was three days later.
“I bumped my hand, and my nails chipped! Please repaint them!”
That was way too soon.
I finally realized that I wouldn’t have time to feel lonely after this.
